title: The Laziest Service Business That Can Make $373/Day+ (From Home)
promo_conflict: The presenter promotes the model and cites his own results; no course, affiliate, or sponsor conflict is disclosed in the cleaned transcript.

stated_problem.quote: They find options that require them to be the one doing the work and the second they stop working, the money stops, too.
stated_problem.speaker: Sergio

idea.name: Remote cleaning business
idea.one_liner: A local cleaning company finds customers and coordinates independent cleaners, earning the spread between the customer’s payment and the cleaner’s pay.
idea.offer: Recurring home cleaning performed by independent cleaners.
idea.revenue_model: Customer pays per clean; the company pays the cleaner and keeps the spread. The speaker claims a 50–60% margin.

key_quotes.quote: You start a local cleaning company, but instead of doing the work yourself, you build a system around independent cleaners.
So, you handle the marketing, the bookings, the customer communication, and the scheduling, and they get to just show up and do what they do best and get the job done.
You basically get to keep a 50 to 60% margin on the job, and the whole thing runs from a laptop.
But, a cleaning customer books every week or every other week, sometimes once a month.
The best performing post that we see working is when you can put a picture of you and your family, you and your dogs, just something that people can resonate with.

claims.claim: The pitch says the business can make $373 a day without employees, equipment, or the owner attending job sites.
claims.quote: $373 a day, no employees, no equipment, no showing up to job sites.

claims.claim: The speaker says he has made hundreds of thousands of dollars with the model.
claims.quote: I've made hundreds of thousands of dollars with this remote cleaning model.

claims.claim: The claimed job margin is 50–60%.
claims.quote: You basically get to keep a 50 to 60% margin on the job, and the whole thing runs from a laptop.

claims.claim: The speaker says customers typically stay 1–2 years and generate thousands of dollars over that period.
claims.quote: And on average, people will usually stay 1 to 2 years, netting you thousands of dollars for that one customer.

claims.claim: A standard home clean is priced at about $300–$350.
claims.quote: A standard home cleaning is about $300 to $350 per clean.

claims.claim: The cleaner is paid about half of the cleaning price, leaving a stated spread of $150–$175 per booking.
claims.quote: And so, you're basically paying the cleaner half of that, and so your spread on every job, on every booking, is going to be around $150 to $175.

claims.claim: The speaker’s example says 2–3 jobs in a day could produce $373 that day.
claims.quote: Stack two or three of those jobs a day, and you're at $373 a day.

claims.claim: The speaker estimates this as roughly $2,600 a month.
claims.quote: That's roughly $2,600 a month from a business that you're not physically having to operate.

claims.claim: The speaker claims a $40 billion cleaning industry and says no single company owns 1% of it.
claims.quote: this industry is worth over $40 billion and no single company owns even 1% of that.

claims.claim: The speaker illustrates cleaner quality by saying perhaps 80 out of 100 cleaners are bad.
claims.quote: if there's 100 cleaners, maybe 80 of them are bad and that's what most people end up having to deal with.

claims.quote: when you reach out to those 100 cleaners and you find the 20 really good cleaners in your city

claims.quote: as long as you don't live in the middle of nowhere and you have a population of at least 50,000 people

claims.quote: If you're a little more tech-savvy, a little more experienced, you can honestly have this business up in a single weekend.

claims.claim: A newer founder might take a week to set up the business.
claims.quote: If you're a little bit newer to business, maybe it takes you a week, but honestly, it shouldn't take you longer than that to get this whole business set up from start to finish.

claims.claim: The speaker says cleaners could be hired within 1–2 weeks and money could be made within 30 days.
claims.quote: You can have your first cleaners hired within a week or two, and you could be making money within the first 30 days, 100%.

claims.quote: What I always say is, really to make your first dollar, all you really need is a way for people to contact you, a good cleaner you can send to the job, and a customer that needs the service done.

claims.claim: A cleaner recruitment post might get 10, 20, or 30 comments.
claims.quote: You are going to get flooded with probably 10, 20, or 30 people commenting.

claims.quote: First, you need at least a year of professional cleaning experience.

claims.claim: The speaker says he avoids spending hundreds of dollars on supplies for cleaners who might leave within a couple of months.
claims.quote: I am not coming out of pocket for hundreds of dollars to give them supplies, especially when I don't know if they're going to be with me for more than, you know, a couple months.

claims.claim: The speaker describes the applicant pool using an 80/20 rule.
claims.quote: Like I said earlier, this is the 80/20 rule.

claims.claim: The described screening process has four steps.
claims.quote: Most of these applicants and people that I talk to are not going to make it through this four-step filter that I just outlined.

claims.claim: The speaker says 2–3 cleaners are enough to do $10,000 a month.
claims.quote: You only need two to three cleaners to do 10K a month.

claims.claim: A low-cost test clean could take around 3 hours and cost $100.
claims.quote: That's basically equal to around 3 hours of work, so you pay them $100.

claims.claim: The speaker says test cleans have saved him tens of thousands of dollars by helping him avoid bad hires.
claims.quote: And so, this is the test clean that has saved me probably tens of thousands of dollars in hiring bad cleaners.

claims.claim: The suggested introductory discount is $50, $100, or as much as 50%.
claims.quote: I'm willing to give you like $50 off, $100 off, or even as extreme as 50% off on your first clean.

claims.claim: The speaker suggests getting five-star reviews after the introductory clean.
claims.quote: And on top of that, you can get testimonials and five-star reviews out of of person afterwards.

claims.claim: The speaker recommends calling within 5–10 minutes after a clean to discuss recurring service.
claims.quote: Now, it's super important that you call them right after the clean was done, like within 5 to 10 minutes.

claims.claim: The speaker says a converted recurring customer is worth thousands of dollars over their lifetime.
claims.quote: And like I said earlier, when a one-time customer converts to recurring, now they're worth thousands of dollars to you over the lifetime of them using your service.

claims.claim: The speaker says this model can build to $10,000 a month.
claims.quote: And through that, you can build a remote cleaning business that makes 10K a month.

acquisition_channels.details: Posts in local Facebook groups or Nextdoor to recruit cleaners, then introduces the cleaning business in local groups to find customers.
DMs people who like or comment on the local introduction post, starts a conversation, and offers a discount.
Asks discounted first-clean customers to tell others in their local group if they like the service.

ideas.delivery: The company handles marketing, bookings, customer communication, and scheduling; independent cleaners bring their own transport and supplies and perform the home cleans. The company handles complaints and may send a cleaner back to fix a bad job.

prices: $50 or $100 off, or up to 50% off the first clean

uk_legal_risk.reason: The described customer funnel DMs local consumers who engage with a post and then offers discounts. Under the requested PECR filter, unsolicited social direct marketing to individuals is a risk.

ideas.other_uk_rules: Check UK GDPR for customer addresses and contact data; Employment Agencies Regulations 2003 and worker-status/tax treatment for cleaners engaged as independent contractors; and consumer contract, cancellation, and potentially DMCC Act subscription requirements for recurring consumer cleans. Screen any unsolicited marketing calls against TPS (and CTPS for corporate subscribers).
